newsitem.title: UK: LME metals explore lower regions of price bands.
newsitem.headline: LME metals explore lower regions of price bands.

text.p: LME copper and aluminium finished Wednesday's afternoon kerb softer, but failed to break out of price bands which have imprisoned the market recently.
Most other metals fell under the moderately bearish influence and also ended the day easier, but business was thin ahead of the long Easter break.
Three months copper slid after failing again at the upside in the morning, stalling at a high of $2,385, the region that has capped prices for the past two weeks.
But the market lacked the steam to break substantially lower, ending the day at its low of $2,352, off $25.
Copper's weakest price this month was on March 19 when it slid to $2,305.
"It's been pretty dull. Everything is still within the basic ranges and easing back to support levels," said analyst Martin Squires of broker Rudolf Wolff.

During the afternoon session, news emerged that Poland's KGHM copper concern and trade unions agreed to boost average wages by 17 percent instead of 15 percent, and the unions agreed to review last week's decision to go on "strike alert".
A massive 203,942 lot turnover in copper options on Tuesday failed to affect the market since participants widely agreed it represented a transfer in positions rather than outright business.
The premium of cash over three months prices was slightly narrower at $53/$58.
Fund profit-taking pressured aluminium, which ended the kerb at $1,632, down $21. The final price was $2 off its low, which was the lowest price since February 21 and below the 30-day moving average.
Balancing the fund liquidation, however, was some forward and trade buying, which was encouraging, Squires said.
Investment funds were also locking in profits and scaling down long positions in nickel, Squires said, adding that the broad uptrends in both metals were still intact.
Nickel finished $145 lower at $7,635.
Support was pegged at $7,600, chartists said.
Lead tried higher, touching $687, but ended just $1 firmer at $680, its 30-day moving average.
The spreads flared a bit, with the cash/threes backwardation about $5 wider at $6/$8. The tightest portion of that structure appeared to be April/May, which was at a $7/$9 backwardation.
Zinc shed $10 to $1,289 after failing to attack the $1,300 level earlier in the day.
Tin finished $20 weaker at $5,825, closing just off its low.
Alloy ended slightly easier at $1,540, down from $1,545/55.
--Eric Onstad, London Newsroom +44 171 542-8065
